name: Reel
text: Adopt **automated risk scoring at ingest with a mandatory override by Data Protection**, enforced by Engineering. This forces correct labeling at the earliest possible point, cutting off mislabeled datasets before they spread and eliminating last-minute disputes. The trade-off is that teams may over-label to avoid downstream friction, but Data Protection’s expertise ensures legal risks are handled correctly upfront—preventing fines and bottlenecks later.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk in Sift’s plan is that Data Protection’s override becomes a rubber stamp—teams will label everything “high-risk” at ingest to avoid downstream friction, clogging Data Protection’s queue with trivial cases while critical exports stall. The better fix is **automated risk scoring at export with a mandatory override by the data owner’s direct manager**, enforced by Engineering. This keeps accountability with the team closest to the data while preventing gaming by forcing them to justify overrides. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with both models and measuring override rates and false positives.
